title: In the Land of AI Agents, the Verifiers Are King — Tariq Shaukat, Sonar
talk_summary: Sonar's CEO argues that AI coding agents produce plausible but buggy, complex, insecure code, and that the productivity gains from agents dissipate within ~3 months unless verification is baked into the agentic loop rather than treated as afterthought code review. He proposes a 'guide, verify, solve' framework with three loops (agentic inner loop, CI/PR verification loop, code-maintenance loop) and zero-trust multi-model verification.

takeaways.what_they_do: Separate 'context' (architectural awareness, semantic navigation maps of the codebase) from 'constraints' (coding standards, allowed/forbidden dependencies, intended target architecture, guardrails) and feed both to agents before generation, so there is less to verify and fix afterward.
takeaways.numbers: >30% reduction in tokens to solve a given problem

takeaways.what_they_do: Deliberately use different models and different techniques (algorithmic checks on data/control flow, secrets, known patterns, plus agentic checks on intent and business logic) rather than one reviewer model, because every model has biases and a 'personality'.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Every model has biases. Every model produces has a character has a personality. So, let's make sure we use different models and different techniques
takeaways.numbers: 44% less frequent AI-derived production outages for multi-layered verification users

takeaways.technique: In-loop verification fed back to the agent
takeaways.what_they_do: Give the agent verification results while it is still working (inner agentic loop) so it fixes problems in the same run, rather than deferring all checking to PR review.
takeaways.evidence_quote: how do you provide the agents as it's generating the code as it's doing the work with the context and constraints with the inloop verification

takeaways.technique: Three explicit loops: agentic, CI verification, code maintenance
takeaways.what_they_do: Design the SDLC as three reinforcing loops with verification at the center: the agent inner loop, a PR/CI verification loop, and a standing code-maintenance loop run by remediation agents.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there's the agentic loop, there's a CI verification loop, there's the code maintenance loop
takeaways.numbers: 92% reduction in issues cited at one large bank using guide/verify/solve in agentic loops

takeaways.what_they_do: Measure the same agentic tasks on a typical vs. cleaned codebase and show materially less tokens, reasoning, and energy needed on the clean one, because agents must understand the code to operate on it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you see a material reduction in the amount of tokens, reasoning, energy, etc. needed for those cleaner uh code bases versus the typical code bases

takeaways.technique: Quality gates / evals as the outer loop
takeaways.what_they_do: Treat evals and quality gates as a distinct outer loop that checks whether the guide/verify/solve system is actually passing, rather than assuming agent output is good.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you have your EV valves and you have your quality gates to check are you actually passing
